### Observed differences

- In the later window, A10 takes part in about 62 in 100 cases, up from about 23 in 100, and its mean occurrences per trace rose from about 0.24 to 0.65. [OCC003]
- A10 now occurs much earlier in the case: its mean relative event position fell from about 0.57 to 0.28 (median from 0.55 to 0.23). [POS001]
- A10's outgoing transitions now lead to A16 in about 91 in 100 of those transitions, up from about 13 in 100, and when A10 is followed by A16 within five steps this is now almost always immediately adjacent (lag-1 share about 97 in 100, up from 55). [DIR002, LAG001]
- A15 is now followed by A10 in about 36 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (previously about 2 in 100), while its share towards A16 fell from about 92 to 64 in 100; about 120 of 200 later-window cases contain A15 followed by A10 within five steps, up from 13. [DIR003, LAG005]
- A10 now precedes the later activities A27, A28, A29, A30, A42, A47 and A48 in about 55–58 in 100 cases (previously about 5–21 in 100) and co-occurs with each of them in about 62 in 100 cases (previously about 23 in 100). [REL007, REL009, REL011, REL012, REL013]
- A19, A20, A25 and A26 have nearly disappeared: each appeared in about 24–26 in 100 cases before and in only about 1–3 in 100 afterwards (for example A19 in 5 of 200 cases and A26 in 2). [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- Accordingly, A15 and A16 now almost never co-occur with these four activities (about 1–3 in 100 cases, down from about 24–26 in 100), and pairs among the four themselves show "neither present" in about 96–98 in 100 cases. [REL014, REL018, REL022, REL041]
- Several successions became near-fixed: A28 to A29 now carries about 96 in 100 of A28's outgoing transitions (from about 50) and A29 to A30 about 98 in 100 (from about 49), with A28 typically reaching A30 two steps later (previously three); A42 to A27, A45 to A46 and A47 to A48 now carry about 96–99 in 100 of their source's outgoing transitions. [DIR008, DIR009, LAG026, LAG030, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012]
- A04 and A06 also receded, from about 17 in 100 cases each to about 5 and 6 in 100, and activities present in every case (A16, A27, A28, A42) shifted slightly later in relative position, by about 0.02–0.03. [OCC001, OCC002, POS002, POS007, POS008, POS009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process was rerouted around A10 while the mid-process group A19, A20, A25 and A26 is now rarely executed: in the later window A10 runs in about three in five cases and much earlier, leads almost exclusively to A16, and precedes the later activities A27, A28, A29, A30, A42, A47 and A48 in about 55–58 in 100 cases, while A19, A20, A25 and A26 — each previously present in about a quarter of cases between A28/A29 and A30 — now appear in only about 1–3 in 100, with flow typically passing from A28 via A29 to A30 without them. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, POS001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR008, DIR009, REL007, LAG001, LAG025, LAG026, LAG030]

This judgement rests on directness and consistency rather than item count alone: the placement change is shown relationally (A10 before the late activities, A15 feeding into A10), not only through frequency shifts; occurrence, routing, position, co-occurrence and gap indicators all point the same way, with large supports (for example 123 cases behind A10's occurrence profile and about 200 outgoing transitions behind the A28 and A29 routing profiles); and 120 qualifying items against roughly 1 expected for an unchanged process is far beyond what chance screening produces. [OCC003, DIR002, POS001, REL007, LAG001, DIR008, DIR009]

An important competing explanation cannot be ruled out: a shift in the mix of pre-existing variants between the two 200-case windows — a later window that simply contains more A10-centred cases and fewer cases running the A19/A20/A25/A26 group — would produce the same participation, routing and order differences without any structural modification. In addition, several gap items about the vanished activities rest on only 1–3 later-window observations and were not relied on. [LAG012, LAG014, LAG022, LAG029, OCC004, DIR005]
